subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Charles Ponzi's Original Scheme
description: A quick, practical guide to Charles Ponzi's Original Scheme.

hook.text: In 1920, an Italian immigrant in Boston promised 50% profit in 45 days. Thousands believed him.

buildup.text: Charles Ponzi claimed he exploited price differences in international postal reply coupons.

discovery.text: The coupon arbitrage was real in theory, but impossible to execute at the scale Ponzi claimed.

twist.text: He collected $20 million — roughly $300 million today — before running out of new investors.

climax.text: When exposed, six banks failed. Ponzi served prison time and was eventually deported to Italy.

punchline.text: His name outlived his fortune — by a century.

quiz.question: What did Charles Ponzi claim to trade?
